sources.name: YouGov: worst president, open-ended pick (2018, 2020, 2021)
sources.method: US adults pick the worst president. Feb 2021: Trump 46%, Obama 24%, Nixon 5% (3rd). Jan 2020 (yougov.com/en-us/articles/27648-americas-best-president-poll): Trump 41, Obama 21, Nixon 3, G.W. Bush 3. Feb 2018 (yougov.com/en-us/articles/20257-ranking-presidents-presidents-day): Trump, Obama, Nixon a distant 3rd, Clinton, G.W. Bush. This measures how readily people name each president, not how much they like him.

changes_vs_current: New topic. The ranking averages each president's position across the 9 people sources (a president missing from a source counts as that list's length + 5). All 12 gut-check picks landed in the top 12 of the raw ranking.

Donald Trump moved from #9 to #8, above Thomas Jefferson. Trump is #2-3 in every open-ended best-president poll (2020, 2021) and 97% famous, but the popularity-based sources pull him down. Jefferson is backed by only 3 sources, so the gut check and the open-ended polls win this swap.

Aliases leave out the ambiguous surnames 'roosevelt', 'bush', 'adams' and 'johnson'. Each president in those pairs gets only distinct forms (fdr / teddy / tr, dubya / w / bush 43 vs bush 41 / hw bush, john adams vs jqa / john quincy adams, lbj).

Coordinator gut check: Richard Nixon moved from #27 (raw average) to #15, just above George W. Bush. The board shows what people name, with no 'greatest' framing. Favorability ranks infamous presidents low, but that doesn't mean people name them less. Nixon is 95% famous in YouGov Ratings (13th of 45 by fame), and he is consistently the #3 open-ended pick for worst president in YouGov polls (2018 distant 3rd; 2020 3%, tied with G.W. Bush; 2021 5%), behind only Trump and Obama. Every president below him on the board is less famous.

John Quincy Adams (#20) dropped to make room. He is 91% famous but appears only in the YouGov Ratings data, never in an open-ended or great/worst poll. 'john adams' already covers most people who would type Adams.
confidence: medium: the top 7 agree strongly across YouGov/Gallup sources, but #13-24 rest mostly on YouGov Ratings popularity and fame plus open-ended worst-president mentions, so the tail order is soft.
